what_happened: The job was meant to hold a job on low disk and resume it automatically, instead of ending it failed. It was rejected at the final verdict. Two of 9 acceptance criteria were unmet. (1) The criterion to run `cargo test -p athena-core` and show the low-disk hold is not counted as a work failure, with idle-build cleanup still running first, was unmet. (2) The criterion that `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass was unmet. There were two blocker or major findings. The blocker: an existing scope-guard test, `a_low_disk_job_is_read_as_an_environment_attempt` (scope_guard.rs:1377-1399), still expects low disk at the verifier gate to close the job Failed, so `cargo test` fails. The major finding: behavior criterion 8's evidence must cite commands that ran (D43). One check failed, and it is a check, not a criterion: `test` failed in athena-cli `backtest.rs:125`. The test `the_real_log_has_no_condition_a_finding_against_the_confirmed_list` reported a condition-a finding, "supersession phrases without a target id at lines [3875]". The stored fields do not say whether this check failure came from the job or was already there.
cause: The job changed the behavior of a core outcome path (low disk at the verifier gate goes from Failed to hold), but nothing during the job makes the full test suite run and pass before the final verdict. The producer was not shown that an existing test pins the old behavior, and nothing lists the tests that read the changed outcome so they can be updated with the code. The criterion about not counting a hold as a work failure was also not tied to the old scope-guard test that contradicts it. Separately, a log-based backtest failed on a real-log line, and no baseline shows whether the job or the existing log caused it, so a possibly unrelated failure can sink the job. Only the verifier at the final verdict runs everything and compares the evidence, and there rejection is the only outcome. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the plan or tests.
prevention: Before the producer's work goes to the verifier, run the full check set (`cargo test`, clippy, fmt) automatically and send any failure back to the producer. At the same time, record a baseline of the same checks on the unchanged base so a failure is attributed to the job or to the base. Add a plan-time step that greps for existing tests of any outcome the job changes (here, the Failed outcome for low disk) and lists them as in-scope edits. Also require each behavior criterion's evidence to cite a command that actually ran, and have the producer's report be checked against that before the verdict.
proposed_request: Re-do "Hold jobs on low disk and auto-resume instead of failing". Outcome: when free disk is too low before the checks or before the verifier, Athena first runs idle-build cleanup, which removes only Athena-owned finished-job directories. If that frees enough space, the job proceeds. If it does not, the job is held (not closed Failed) and resumes automatically when space returns. A low-disk hold must not count as a work failure in introspection, failure classes or the scope guard. Allowed changes: the production code for the hold, and the existing tests that pin the old behavior, including watcher_tests::a_low_disk_job_is_read_as_an_environment_attempt in scope_guard.rs, which must be updated to the new hold outcome. Acceptance: (1) a test in athena-core shows a low-disk hold before the checks and before the verifier is not counted in introspection, failure classes or the scope guard; (2) a test shows idle-build cleanup runs first and lets the job proceed when it frees enough space, and removes only Athena-owned finished-job directories; (3) `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass, and the report cites each command run with its result; (4) if athena-cli backtest `the_real_log_has_no_condition_a_finding_against_the_confirmed_list` fails, first run it on the unchanged base and report whether the failure was already there, and do not change unrelated log content to hide it.
